card.name: Punctuation and links in warning headings
card.fires_on: Closing parentheses, commas, colons or semicolons, and a few linking words like "of" or "can", right where a warnings section ends a cross-reference or turns to a new risk heading. Seen in highlights text with section numbers such as (5.2).

modes.label: After section numbers
modes.description: A closing parenthesis or comma inside a list of section cross-references.
modes.example: monitor for hemodynamic changes after initiating or increasing the dosage of dronabinol oral solution. ( 5.2<< )>> Interaction with Disulfiram and Metron

modes.label: Boxed warning titles
modes.description: A colon or semicolon in an all-caps boxed warning title, just before the next risk name.
modes.example: WARNING: ADDICTION, ABUSE, AND MISUSE; LIFE-THREATENING RESPIRATORY DEPRESSION<<;>> ACCIDENTAL INGESTION; MED

modes.label: Linking word before a risk
modes.description: A short verb or preposition that leads into a named risk or effect.

card.plain: It fires on the small punctuation and linking words in warning headings that come just before a named risk.
